residual_risks: This spike composes three previously sealed spikes at the TEST level rather than building one unified, production-shaped 'governed read' pipeline object; each backend's non-interference proof is real and independent, but nothing here yet demonstrates a single in-process call spanning all three backends in one governed request -- that would be an integration task, not a spike, and is out of this task's scope per its own implementation_procedure ('add the smallest contract-compliant implementation').

The Jena axis models compartments via classification labels (UNCLASSIFIED/SECRET/TOP_SECRET, the same scheme OCOR-DEV-0018 already used); the Qdrant axis models compartments via named partitions (low/high); these are two different, backend-appropriate compartment representations, not a single cross-backend compartment identifier -- unifying them is a design decision reserved for whichever future task actually builds the integrated pipeline.

The OPA/OpenBao cross-service timing test proves non-interference for ONE pairing (pausing OpenBao while probing OPA); it does not exhaustively test every pair of the four sealed identity/policy controls, which would multiply real fault-injection cycles without adding a materially different proof technique.
The same pre-existing local-venv gap noted in prior evidence (uv cannot resolve the exact 3.12.11 interpreter in this sandbox) is unchanged and out of this task's scope.
rollback_procedure_verified: Every test either resets its backend fixture at the start (Jena) or is scoped to a freshly self-provisioned and torn-down Qdrant container (the qdrant_campaign fixture's finally-block destroy), so a failed assertion never leaves durable cross-test state; the OpenBao pause/unpause cycle recovers in a finally block before its own assertions run, verified directly by the post-run check that no self-provisioned Qdrant containers were left behind and the persistent 11-service stack remained healthy across 4 consecutive full test-suite runs.
